_about: The hotel test's project file (2 Nov 2026): the owner's facts, the decisions and the assumptions build_model.py uses with takeoff.json. Keys that start with '_' are notes. Second round (2 Nov, afternoon): the owner's answers to the first build's questions and the review's fixes.
project: Hotel ground floor and floor 2 (from two pictures)

owner.floors: the first picture is floor 1 and the second is floor 2
owner.liftDoor: the entrance of the lift is 1 metre (the lift door opening); rough
owner.stairWidth: one real dimension: stair width 2500 mm (the main stair: floor 1's flight between its two brown side walls, arriving at floor 2's middle 'iconic staircase')
owner.stairs: the middle stair is going down to floor 1; the upper one (beside the toilets) is going up to floor 3
owner.faceted: the large white faceted shape in the middle of floor 2 is a seating
owner.checkIn: after the first page (2 Nov): the purple boxes it called laptop / monitor are seat backs, not screens (a monitor on the sofa makes no sense): the round shape and the rectangle at floor 1's check-in are seating

scale._method: 'stair' (the owner's one real dimension, the main reference): floor 1's flight is 2.50 m wide between its side walls' inner faces (read_pictures rule 11), along floor 1's x. 'cores': the four lift doors average liftDoor; 'doors-floor1': floor 1's two lift doors are liftDoor (both kept for comparison, hotel_summary.json scale.otherMethods).
scale._axes: 'per-axis': the ratio between the pictures' scales from the lift core's faces, one per axis (x 1.409, y 1.354: floor 1 is drawn 4 % wider than tall against floor 2; its big round sofa 2.9 %, its lift shafts 5 % against 1.4 % on floor 2); floor 2 is taken as drawn square. 'one': a single ratio for both axes (the first build).

defaults._doorHead: assumed, every door including the lift doors (no elevations)
defaults._liftDoorWidth: the owner (2 Nov): every lift door opening is built exactly this wide, centred on the drawn gap
defaults._risers: the stairs: FL to FL 2.90 m / 17 = 0.171 m per riser (floor 1 to floor 2, and floor 2's flight up to floor 3)
defaults._railingHeight: assumed, as in the bank (the edges of the open stair on floor 2)
defaults._terraceRailingHeight: assumed: the railing on floor 2's terrace's open edges
defaults._hatch: assumed: the serving hatch and the food lift's hatch are open from 0.90 m to 2.10 m (the door head); a hatch with a counter standing in it has its sill at the counter's top instead (the serving hatch F2-014: 0.85 m, the counter's height, so the counter reads flush through it)
defaults._pictureEdgeWall: assumed: where the picture cuts the building off and the floor would end in the air (floor 2's back of house at the top edge), a full-height wall this thick closes it, just beyond the picture's edge
defaults._glassThickness: assumed: the glazing is a pane in a frame, built 5 cm thick, full height

assumptions: Scale (2 Nov, the owner's one real dimension): floor 1's main stair is 2.50 m wide, taken as the CLEAR width of the flight between its two brown side walls, at their inner faces (the centres of their outline strokes, measured on rows clear of the red 'Luggage storage' box, which is drawn on those faces): 148.19 px, so floor 1 is 59.28 px per metre along x. At that reading floor 1's armchairs are about 0.7 m and its sofa about 1.85 m; measured over the side walls they would be 0.6 m and 1.5 m.

Scale per axis: the two pictures draw one lift core, and its faces (stroke centres) give the ratio between the pictures' scales per axis: x 1.4095, y 1.3539 (floor 1 is drawn 4.1 % wider than tall against floor 2; its big round sofa is 2.9 % wider than tall, its lift shafts 5 % against floor 2's 1.4 %). Floor 2 is taken as drawn square (its round tables are round within their noise): 42.06 px/m on floor 2, 59.28 x 56.94 px/m on floor 1. The cores then stack within 0.034 m (2.0 px of floor 1; with one ratio 4.5 px).

Checks of the scale (the owner's 1 m lift door is rough): measured at the nibs' faces (stroke centres), the drawn lift openings come out 1.12 m on floor 1 and 1.25-1.28 m on floor 2; each lift door is built exactly 1.00 m wide on its drawn centre, with wall back at its two ends. Floor 2 draws its iconic staircase 2.74 m between its stringers' inner lines and 2.930 m over them, which is floor 1's flight over its side walls (2.934 m), and the two outlines stack within 3 cm: floor 2 draws the stair's outline over floor 1's side walls.
Levels 0.00 and +2.90 m (the owner's FL to FL); walls 2.90 m high on both floors, up to the next floor (floor 3 is not in the pictures).

Walls are as thick as their outline strokes are apart (face to face at the strokes' centres), with straight faces fitted to the straight runs; the red annotation strokes are painted over with the colour around them first, so the stair walls and the north wall come out straight and closed.
Slab 0.20 m under each floor; door heads 2.10 m, a lintel above each door to the top of the wall, a glass transom over the ENTRY door, which stands between glass.

Glass, 5 cm thick and full height: floor 1's south facade (a thin line; its mullions are the dark ticks drawn on it, 0.22-0.27 m wide), the core's two south windows (white strips between piers), floor 2's side of the bar to the terrace (a thin double line with a light fill). Floor 2's west facade is wall (the owner, 2 Nov).
The RED BOX vestibule's walls (two dark strokes about 3 px apart: about 6 cm) and the stair's two side walls on floor 1 (drawn timber brown, 0.22 m) are full-height walls.

The middle stair (the owner: it goes down from floor 2 to floor 1) is built as 17 risers of 0.171 m and 16 goings of 0.27 m between the side walls' inner faces (2.50 m), from floor 2's void edge where its bench stands to the arrival edge at floor 2's north end. Floor 1 draws its lowest tread line 0.24 m further south (its 14 lines 0.40 m apart are schematic): the bottom riser is put on floor 2's void edge so that no step runs under floor 2's slab.

Floor 2 is open over floor 1's flight, the opening fitted to it (2.50 m between the side walls' inner faces, from the bottom riser to the top one), with 1.10 m railings standing on the slab at its west, east and south edges (the south one is not drawn: the bench stands there, but the drop is 2.90 m). Floor 1's side walls rise under the slab's edges, so no slot opens beside the flight. No tread line is drawn over the opening.

The upper stair beside the toilets goes up to a floor 3 that is not in the pictures (the owner): its 8 drawn riser lines are built as 7 solid steps rising north from floor 2 (0.171 m risers, 0.32 m goings), ending in the air at +1.19 m, between its side walls' inner faces (2.75 m clear, as drawn); the grey landing north of them is left at floor 2's level, where the FEMALE door F2-006 opens (the picture puts that door on the landing). The wall between it and the FEMALE toilet is drawn as a light band on the teal with a dark stroke on the stair side (0.18 m).

The outside stair: its tread lines lie flat on the floor (it is not known whether it goes up or down to the street); the spine between its two flights (drawn faintly, like the tread lines, 0.48 m) is a low wall at railing height (1.10 m), not a full-height wall; one west wall, the outer line (the inner double line, drawn like the spine, is read as a kerb or rail line on the landing).

Floor 2 is open over the two lift shafts, the small shaft and a small duct beside lift 2. The food lift is a dumbwaiter: its floor is closed, with a hatch on its north side (the light strip, like floor 1's lift-door panels), facing the food lift lobby.

The white strip in the pantry's south wall, facing the canteen counter's north leg, is a serving hatch, open from the pantry counter's top (0.85 m) to 2.10 m. The white strip east of the food lift stands against a wall the picture draws solid: it is a worktop in the back room, not a second hatch (the second review, 2 Nov).

Floor plates: floor 1 is the inside of its walls and glazing with the RED BOX. Floor 1's forecourt paving, from the facade to the road at the paving's south edge (where the traffic arrows start), is an outdoor floor at 0.00, so the RED BOX's outer doors open onto floor (the thin rounded line in the paving is not its edge). Floor 2 includes the pantry, the outside stair's enclosure and the outdoor terrace, which runs on past the picture's edges to the outline floor 1 dashes for the floor above (its south line 0.42 m beyond floor 2's bottom edge, its east line 0.54 m beyond its right edge), from floor 2's own west edge and, east of the facade, from the grey band's north edge; a 1.10 m railing stands on the terrace's open edges, run on to the walls at its ends. The floor goes on beyond floor 2's top edge (the back of house, the toilets): not modelled; where the cut edge is open (from the pantry's west wall to the east facade) a full-height wall, 0.15 m, closes it just beyond the edge, labelled 'picture edge (the drawing stops here; assumed closed)', so nobody walks off it.
Walls drawn as light lines (the pantry's on its dark fill, the toilets' on teal) are read by eye as bands 0.12 to 0.24 m thick.

Room names stand where their hand lettering or red callout is; Car park and Entrance lie outside floor 1's plate, as their labels do. 'Luggage storage' (the red box drawn over the lower half of the flight) is put at the north end of the flight, where the high steps leave headroom underneath (the owner can say otherwise).

Furniture: the kind of each piece by what it looks like; the family is a short name (what the 3D team swaps models by), remarks are in the note. The faceted white form on floor 2 is sculptural seating (the owner), kind seat, 450 mm, followed by 3 boxes. At floor 1's check-in the big round shape is a round sofa and the rectangle beside it a sofa (the owner, after the first page; its family is 'check-in sofa', so that 'sofa' means only floor 2's sofas, whose backs are in their box), both kind seat, 450 mm (the seat), and the five bars drawn on them, first read as a monitor and four self check-in screens, are their seat backs, kind seat-back, 800 mm, standing on the floor where they are drawn, at the seats' rims, on nothing: a kind's height is shared by all its boxes, so the seats are not kind sofa, whose 800 mm box would hide their own 800 mm backs. The circles with a cross (2 on floor 1, 3 on floor 2 beside seats, 7 on the dining table) are the usual symbol of ceiling or pendant lights: not furniture boxes (the owner can say otherwise); the faint square with a cross in floor 2's lift lobby is a glyph of the printed background drawing. The art work on floor 1 is a panel on the wall, not a box.

Left out as annotation: the red callout lines and dots (their words kept as room names), the black traffic arrows, the dashed site lines (floor 1's dashed outline of the floor above is used for the terrace's edge), the bar zone's dashed outline, the faint printed text of the underlying drawings.

furniture._heights: every kind keeps the kit's office default (the circles with a cross are lights, not lamps: no lamp kind is left, so the 1600 mm floor-lamp height of the first build is gone; seat 450 mm for the sculptural seating and the check-in's round sofa and sofa, seat back 800 mm for their backs)
